description: This topic is based on the sequence of letters, numbers, and symbols. It evaluates a candidate's logical ability, calculation speed, and accuracy.

sections.title: Positional Values of Letters
sections.description: The English Alphabet consists of 26 letters. Memorizing the forward and backward positional values of letters is essential for solving questions quickly.

key_concepts.explanation: This is a shortcut technique used to remember the positional values of letters in multiples of 5.
When the sum of the positional values of two letters is exactly 27, they are considered opposite to each other in the alphabet.

sections.title: Finding Position in a Series
sections.description: Rules for determining the exact position of a specific element from the left or right end within a given sequence.

results: Left to Left: Subtract the positions (L1 - L2) and count from the left end.
Right to Right: Subtract the positions (R1 - R2) and count from the right end.
Left to Right: Add the positions (L + R) and count from the left end.
Right to Left: Add the positions (R + L) and count from the right end.

sections.title: Preceded and Followed Elements
sections.description: Techniques for locating specific elements in an alphanumeric series based on given immediate sequence conditions.

key_concepts.notation_or_symbol: X Y (Y is preceded by X)
key_concepts.explanation: This term means 'immediately before'. If an element is placed right before another element, it is said to precede it.

key_concepts.notation_or_symbol: Y Z (Y is followed by Z)
key_concepts.explanation: This term means 'immediately after'. If an element is placed right after another element, it is said to follow it.

sections.title: Finding Letter Pairs
sections.description: The process of counting the number of letter pairs in a given word that have the same number of letters between them as in the English alphabetical series.

steps.title: Write Positional Values
steps.detail: Write down the numerical values of all the letters in the word according to their standard English alphabetical order.

steps.title: Count Forward and Backward
steps.detail: Start counting alphabetically from each letter in both directions: from left to right and from right to left.

steps.title: Identify Pairs
steps.detail: When the letter you speak during your count matches the actual letter present in the word, it forms a valid letter pair.

sections.title: Dictionary Order and Meaningful Words
sections.description: Arranging words logically or combining extracted letters to form new, meaningful vocabulary.

results: Arrange the words in strict alphabetical order based on their first letter.
If the first letters are identical, compare the second letters, and continue this process sequentially.
Extract the specifically indicated letters from the given word.
Rearrange these extracted letters in various combinations to determine how many valid English words can be formed.
